purpose: Stronger baselines than the rule arm: greedy (fixed-order evaluation) and random (deterministic seeded shuffle). Both bypass the agent harness and drive evaluate_candidates directly, so they are honest offline evaluators with no planning.
frozen_version: compare_2d_policies.py was extended to add BaselinePolicy and run_baseline(); this changes source_hashes, so this is a new frozen version that cannot be compared directly to the earlier agent-only observations except by metric.

connectivity_gate.note: Baselines are offline, no gate needed

design.greedy: sort unique products by (-catalogue_id_count, smiles); evaluate in that order until budget exhausted
design.random: deterministic seeded shuffle (seed=42); same evaluation loop
design.budget: max_evaluations=11 (1 parent + 10 products); same as agent arm
design.stop_rule: after budget: finish with the best qualifying product, or honestly report none

observations.what: Greedy baseline found no qualifying product on any parent
observations.evidence: phenol greedy qual=0 best=0.00707; aniline greedy qual=0 best=-0.00187; toluene greedy qual=0 best=0.00918 (all below 0.01 threshold)
observations.status: Greedy ordering is not enough: with budget=10 products, the top candidates in the deterministic order never cross the 0.01 threshold.

observations.what: Random baseline finds qualifying on 2/3 parents
observations.evidence: phenol random qual=0 best=0.00706 (still below threshold); aniline random qual=1 best=0.01469; toluene random qual=2 best=0.01355
observations.status: Order matters even with the same evaluator. Random ordering reaches good products that greedy misses.

observations.evidence: agent 4 observations: quals=[0,2,0,1] goal_met=2/4; random single run: qual=1 best=0.01469 (== agent r4 best).
observations.status: Agent reaches 2/4 goal_met on aniline; random reaches 1/1. The same best delta 0.01469 is the best aniline r4 found, suggesting random reaches a real product. Agent's r2 found 2 qualifying with best 0.01698, which random does not.

observations.evidence: agent 4/4 goal_met with best 0.01874 (consistent); random qual=2 best=0.01355.
observations.status: Agent's toluene best (0.01874) is higher than random's best (0.01355) and reproducible across 4 observations. Agent is not just lucky.

observations.evidence: agent 2/4 goal_met with best 0.01744; random qual=0 best=0.00706; greedy qual=0 best=0.00707.
observations.status: Phenol is the hardest parent: even with the agent, only 2/4 reach goal_met, and neither baseline does. The same molecule (or family) appears in agent r2 (best 0.01478) and agent r4 (best 0.01744); neither baseline reaches it.

observations.what: What does the agent add beyond random?
observations.evidence: Agent exceeds random on toluene (best 0.01874 vs 0.01355) and on phenol (agent 2/4 goal_met, random 0/1). On aniline the comparison is closer (agent 2/4 vs random 1/1). Without the agent, greedy finds nothing on any parent.
observations.status: Honest ranking from this single pair of observations: agent > random >> greedy. The agent's contribution is largest on toluene where it consistently finds the same best product, and smallest on phenol where even the agent only finds a qualifying product in 2/4 observations.

honest_limitations: One run per baseline per parent; only one random seed (42). Variance unknown.
Baseline does NOT use planning; it is an upper bound on what a no-decision evaluator can do.

Agent 4-observation results were collected on a previous frozen version; baseline runs are on a new frozen version that includes the BaselinePolicy code. The catalogues are identical, so the scores are comparable, but the source hashes are different.
Random ordering with seed=42 may be lucky or unlucky on specific parents; one run cannot be summarised as 'random finds N% of qualifying products'.
No docking, no biological validation, and the 0.01 threshold is unchanged.
